headline: High Sierra Seasonal Access and Permits
reservation: Devils Postpile and Reds Meadow require a shuttle during peak summer; check NPS for operating dates. Wilderness permits are mandatory for overnight stays and must be reserved through recreation.gov well in advance.

days.title: The Lakes Basin

stops.name: Lake Mary
stops.detail: Enjoy the largest lake in the basin for shoreline walking and views of Crystal Crag.

stops.name: Twin Lakes
stops.detail: See the dramatic waterfall that connects the upper and lower lakes near the base of the mountain.

days.driving: Allow 20–30 minutes; parking is limited at Lake George and Lake Mary
days.note: Altitude adjustment is necessary; the basin sits above 8,000 feet.

days.title: Volcanic Geology and Waterfalls

stops.name: Devils Postpile National Monument
stops.detail: Marvel at the rare 60-foot basalt columns formed by cooling lava thousands of years ago.

stops.name: Rainbow Falls
stops.detail: Follow the trail from the Postpile to see the 101-foot drop of the San Joaquin River.

days.driving: Allow 45–60 minutes via mandatory shuttle during peak summer months
days.note: Check the NPS website for Reds Meadow Road reconstruction schedules which may impact access.

days.title: Eastern Sierra Scenic Loop

stops.name: Convict Lake
stops.detail: Walk the loop trail around this bright blue lake framed by the steep peaks of the Sierra.

stops.name: June Lake Loop
stops.detail: Drive the scenic horseshoe-shaped canyon to view Grant, Silver, and Gull Lakes.

days.driving: Allow 1.5–2 hours for the full loop; conditions vary with mountain weather
days.note: Fall color usually peaks in late September or October depending on elevation.

intel.title: Lakes Basin Demand
intel.text: Parking lots at Lake George and Horseshoe Lake often fill by 10 AM on summer weekends. Use the free town trolley to access popular trailheads without a car.

intel.title: High Elevation Service
intel.text: Service is reliable in town but vanishes once you enter the Lakes Basin or Reds Meadow. Carry paper maps for any hiking beyond the paved lake paths.

intel.title: Mountain Town Supplies
intel.text: Mammoth Lakes has several stations, but prices are typically lower in Bishop. Refuel before heading north toward Lee Vining or the remote backcountry.

intel.title: Summer Shuttle Window
intel.text: The mandatory Reds Meadow shuttle typically runs from late June through Labor Day. Outside these dates, verify if the road is open to private vehicles.

intel.title: Bear Country Protocol
intel.text: Black bears are active in all residential and recreation areas. Use bear-proof lockers for all scented items and never leave food in your vehicle.

plan.arrival: Arrive via US-395; if flying into MMH, arrange a shuttle or rental in advance as local taxi services are limited.
plan.vehicle: High-clearance vehicles are not required for main roads, but winter travel requires snow chains or 4WD per Caltrans regulations.
plan.goldenHour: Minaret Vista offers a premier sunset view of the Ritter Range, though afternoon thunderstorms can obscure the peaks in summer.
